stories-28-38-42-pharaoh-ordering-haman-.title: Pharaoh Ordering Haman to Bake Clay Bricks and Build a Tower to Heaven
stories-28-38-42-pharaoh-ordering-haman-.note: Surah 28:38–42 portrays Pharaoh in Egypt ordering Haman to bake clay bricks and build a lofty tower to climb to the God of Moses, combining the baked-brick tower of Babel (Genesis 11:3–4; Sanhedrin 109a) with Haman from the Persian court of Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators and modern harmonizers propose that Haman was either an unrecorded Egyptian court minister or a title of an Egyptian quarry official distinct from the Persian vizier in the Book of Esther.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Haman the Agagite serves King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) in fifth-century BC Persia (Esther 3:1), roughly a millennium after Moses and Pharaoh in New Kingdom Egypt. Furthermore, firing clay bricks in a kiln to build a tower reaching the heavens is the specific architectural motif of Mesopotamia's Tower of Babel in Genesis 11:3–4 rather than Egyptian stone masonry.

stories-28-38-42-pharaoh-ordering-haman-.quranEn: [38] Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses. Surely I think he is indeed one of the liars.’ [39] He and his forces became arrogant on the earth without any right, and thought that they would not be returned to Us. [40] So We seized him and his forces, and tossed them into the sea. See how the end was for the evildoers! [41] We made them leaders (who) call (others) to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. [42] We pursued them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the scorned.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses.

stories-28-76-82-korah-qarun-heavy-treas.title: Korah (Qarun) Whose Treasure Keys Burdened a Troop of Men in Sanhedrin 110a
stories-28-76-82-korah-qarun-heavy-treas.note: Surah 28:76–82 states that Qarun (Korah) among the people of Moses possessed treasures whose keys burdened a company of strong men before the earth swallowed him, matching Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators explain that God granted Qarun vast wealth among the Israelites in Egypt or the wilderness, and al-Tabari transmits reports that his leather treasury keys required dozens of mule-loads to carry.
discussion.reply: In Numbers 16:1–33, Korah leads a Levitical priesthood dispute against Moses and Aaron without any mention of vast monetary wealth or heavy treasury keys. The detail that the keys (`aklidei`) to Korah's treasuries were a load requiring three hundred white mules originates in the rabbinic aggadah of Rabbi Levi in Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

stories-28-76-82-korah-qarun-heavy-treas.quranEn: [76] Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength. (Remember) when his people said to him, ‘Do not gloat! Surely God does not love those who gloat. [77] But seek the Home of the Hereafter by means of what God has given you, and do not forget your portion of this world. Do good, as God has done good to you, and do not seek to foment corruption on the earth. Surely God does not love the fomenters of corruption.’ [78] He said, ‘I have been given it only because of the knowledge (that is) in me.’ Did he not know that God had destroyed those of the generations before him who were stronger than him and had accumulated more? The sinners will not be questioned about their sins. [79] So he went forth to his people in his splendor. Those who desired this present life said, ‘Would that we had the same as what has been given to Qārūn! Surely he is indeed the possessor of great good luck.’ [80] But those to whom knowledge had been given said, ‘Woe to you! The reward of God is better for the one who believes and does righteousness. But no one will obtain it except the patient.’ [81] So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and he had no cohort to help him, other than God, and he was not one of those who could help themselves. [82] In the morning those who had longed (to be in) his place the day before were saying, ‘Woe (to Qārūn)! Surely God extends (His) provision to whomever He pleases of His servants, and restricts (it). If God had not bestowed favor on us, He would indeed have caused (the earth) to swallow us (too). Woe to him! The disbelievers will not prosper.’
quranHighlights: Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength.

stories-28-3-6-pharaoh-slaughtering-sons.title: Pharaoh Slaughtering Israelite Sons Beside Haman and Their Hosts in Egypt
stories-28-3-6-pharaoh-slaughtering-sons.note: Surah 28:3–6 recounts Pharaoh slaughtering Israelite sons while sparing their women, and pairs Haman and his forces (Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-junudahuma) directly with Pharaoh during the Exodus 1 infanticide, combining Exodus 1:16–22 and Esther 3:1–6.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir identify Haman in 28:6 as Pharaoh's chief minister and advisor in Egypt during the oppression of the Israelites, distinguishing him from the Persian Haman of the Book of Esther or treating the name as an Egyptian court title.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 1:16–22 and Talmud Bavli Sotah 12a, Pharaoh decrees that newborn Hebrew males be cast into the Nile without any minister named Haman. Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite appears a millennium later in Esther 3:1–6 as the grand vizier of the fifth-century BC Persian king Artaxerxes/Ahasuerus in Susa who plotted to exterminate the Jews of the Persian Empire.

stories-28-3-6-pharaoh-slaughtering-sons.quranEn: [3] We recite to you some of the story of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, for a people who believe: [4] Surely Pharaoh had exalted himself on the earth, and divided its people (into) parties, weakening one contingent of them (by) slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. Surely he was one of the fomenters of corruption. [5] But We wanted to bestow favor on those who were weak on the earth, and make them leaders, and make them the inheritors, [6] and to establish them on the earth, and show Pharaoh and Haman, and their forces, what they had to beware of from them.
quranHighlights: weakening one contingent of them (by) slaughtering their sons and sparing their women
and show Pharaoh and Haman, and their forces, what they had to beware of from them

sources.title: Esther (Septuagint LXX)
sources.en: And after this king Artaxerxes highly honored Aman [son] of Amadathes, the Bugaean, and exalted him, and set his seat above all his friends. And all in the palace did him obeisance, for so the king had given orders to do: but Mardochaeus did not do him obeisance. And they in the king's palace said to Mardochaeus, Mardochaeus, why do you transgress the commands of the king? [Thus] they spoke daily to him, but he listened not to them; so they represented to Aman that Mardochaeus resisted the commands of the king: and Mardochaeus had shown to them that he was a Jew. And when Aman understood that Mardochaeus did not obeisance to him, he was greatly enraged, and took counsel to destroy utterly all the Jews who were under the rule of Artaxerxes.
